items.title: scripts/nexus_engineer_tool_gate.py (PreToolUse hook) resolves its own script path relative to CWD -- an accidental cd outside the worktree permanently breaks the engineer session's Bash tool
items.target: RESOLVED 2026-09-09 (commit 624cd68): scripts/orchestrator.py::_spawn_engineer now exports NEXUS_WORKTREE_ROOT into the engineer environment; .claude/nexus-engineer.settings.json's PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook commands resolve against "${NEXUS_WORKTREE_ROOT:-.}" instead of a bare relative path. Recurred 3x live before the fix (NXS-LOCAL-0027, 0030, 0031), each losing self-merge/push ability until the Product Owner intervened by hand.
items.note: NXS-LOCAL-0027's engineer accidentally `cd`-ed into the sibling directory /Users/OzanDur/Codo/neXus/relay (outside its own worktree). The GOV.PO.3 PreToolUse hook (scripts/nexus_engineer_tool_gate.py) resolves its own script path relative to the current working directory rather than an absolute/fixed path, so once CWD changed the hook could no longer even launch -- permanently disabling the Bash tool for the rest of that session (confirmed reproducible via a fresh subagent hitting the identical failure). EnterWorktree(path=...) back into the worktree was also denied (no human approval surface available in an unattended engineer session). Consequence: all work was completed and committed locally, but git push / gh pr create / the standing relay#13 self-merge could not run -- the Product Owner had to push and open the PR manually the next session. Fix direction (not yet designed): the hook should resolve its own script location from something CWD-independent (e.g. the hook's own __file__ path, or an absolute path baked into the PreToolUse config at spawn time) so a stray cd cannot break it; consider also whether the engineer prompt should warn against cd-ing outside the worktree at all.

items.title: PAN HA pair operational identity should consider serial, not just hostname
items.note: OP.0a.P7's PAN HA peer-pairing identity closure (docs/history/phase/OP_0A_PAN_HA_PEER_PAIRING_IDENTITY_CLOSURE.md) found that PAN entity identity (utils.restore_readiness.resolve_entity_id) is hostname-based; hostname is mutable (admin rename), unlike serial, which is already collected on every PAN row in both parsers and already used elsewhere in configuration/panorama_config_collector.py (_collect_direct_compare's identity_mismatch check) as this codebase's own precedent for authoritative device identity. The pairing closure deliberately did not migrate entity_id to serial -- too large a change for a narrow fix, touching every PAN entity_id consumer and existing tests. A deliberate identity-hardening decision belongs before OP.2's identity gate (FAILOVER_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md section 10.1) can depend on PAN pair identity being stable under any real-world hostname change. UPDATE 2026-09-09 (PAN_HA_SERIAL_IDENTITY_HARDENING_DECISION_DOCUMENT, relay NXS-LOCAL-0039): decision document at docs/design/PAN_HA_SERIAL_IDENTITY_HARDENING_DECISION.md. Nine real non-test consumers of resolve_entity_id found by grep (utils/restore_readiness.py, utils/recovery_validation.py, utils/recovery_collect.py, utils/failover/assessment.py x4 call sites, application/workflows/preflight.py, console/app.py), plus three persisted-record consumers of its output value (utils/recovery_store.py's on-disk vault path, utils/config_storage.py/config_history.py's snapshot lookup key, utils/operate/store.py's lock/quarantine key). Key finding: FAILOVER_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md section 10.1 item 2 ('PAN requires the serial identity gate') names a fresh execution-time verification, not a resolve_entity_id namespace migration -- that gate already exists in nascent form (panorama/preflight_collector.py's P1 identity gate, exact-string serial comparison, distinct from the hostname-based physical_device_identity label) -- so the backlog note's framing conflates two separable questions (Q-A: should the collector-identity namespace migrate to serial; Q-B: does OP.2's gate requirement already need that). A hostname-rename-in-place DOES need a data migration for already-persisted records, independent of which option is chosen -- sketched (design only) in the document section 6: recovery vault directories and config-history keys fork at the rename boundary today with zero reconciliation mechanism for PAN (the M8 device_identity_relationships supersession mechanism exists but is CP-only, VENDOR_NAMESPACES=('checkpoint',)). NOT FREEZABLE NOW: three independent PO-level reasons -- (1) the Q-A/Q-B scope-fit question itself, (2) the open P0 pan_serial_representation_identity_evidence_closure item (AWAITING_PO, real-environment MATCH/MISMATCH anomaly on the same serial-identity comparison, root cause unknown) directly undercuts trusting serial as a foundation right now, (3) the persisted-record migration is substantial cross-cutting engineering work needing its own contract. Preliminary lean (not a freeze-ready recommendation): narrow any near-term fix to hardening the existing execution-time serial gate (Option C in the document) rather than migrating resolve_entity_id, but this does not resolve reasons 1 or 2. Disposition: RELAY_NOTE / AWAITING_PO appended to relay/NXS-LOCAL-0039-*.json requesting a PO DECIDE episode before either Option A/B/C is adopted.

items.title: CP SSH host-key trust: mandatory strict enforcement for production/container runtime
items.priority: P0 -- production-blocking before production deployment / CLASS 2
items.note: PO decision 2026-09-03 (OP_0B_1_COMMAND_GATE_PACKAGE.md "CP SSH trust -- PO override, development compatibility mode"): the OP.0b S5 CP HA preflight feature (checkpoint.preflight_collector.run_cp_preflight) defaults strict_host_key=False for the current development/pre-production phase, matching every other CP SSH caller's existing compatibility-mode default -- mandatory strict enforcement is deliberately deferred to the future production/container-pod runtime, not implemented now, to avoid investing in workstation-specific Paramiko trust-management machinery ahead of that migration. Strict mode itself remains fully implemented, fail-closed and selectable today via strict_host_key=True; utils.cp_ssh_trust.apply_strict_host_key_policy is unchanged. This item is the production checklist for closing that deferral. Scope: (1) mandatory strict host-key verification for the production runtime -- no compatibility-mode default once containerized; (2) container/pod known_hosts provisioning mechanism (bind-mount or equivalent, matching deploy/secrets/ conventions); (3) independently verified host-key enrollment/provisioning procedure -- no TOFU, no ssh-keyscan-as-trust, out-of-band fingerprint verification required; (4) host-key rotation procedure; (5) mismatch handling (BadHostKeyException stays a distinct, non-retryable, fail-closed rejection); (6) missing-host-key handling (HostKeyNotTrustedError stays a distinct, non-retryable, fail-closed rejection -- see host-key-retry-classification finding below); (7) no automatic promotion of an OBSERVED_UNVERIFIED compatibility-mode fingerprint to trusted status, ever; (8) production startup/preflight should positively prove trusted host-key material exists before the runtime is considered ready, not merely fail closed on first connection attempt; (9) migration away from workstation-specific trust assumptions (a developer's own ~/.ssh/known_hosts) toward a runtime-owned, deployment-provisioned trust store. Host-key-retry-classification finding folded in here rather than a separate item: op0b_s8_host_key_retry_classification (HostKeyNotTrustedError, merged 2026-09-03, PR #47) already made a missing-host-key rejection non-retryable in both CP SSH retry loops; this item tracks keeping that guarantee true as production hardening proceeds, not redoing it. Reconciled with, not duplicating, the narrower cp_ssh_trust_r2_prod_server item (DEPLOY.1 Ubuntu/Docker server R2 validation for the existing CP config-collection path) -- that item's obligation is one line item under this broader checklist. Do not claim strict production hardening is complete until this item closes; the current state is deliberately, explicitly INCOMPLETE by PO decision, not a regression.

items.title: Render harness's happy-dom check failed under Bun (window.eval undefined)
items.target: before RB.5 (or any next UI build)
items.note: AUTOMATED_VALIDATED 2026-08-31 (contract: docs/history/phase/PHASE0_6_X_RENDER_HARNESS_HAPPYDOM_PIN.md). Root cause was NOT a happy-dom version regression as originally suspected 2026-08-30 -- it is a Bun/node:vm incompatibility. happy-dom executes each Window's script inside a node:vm context; under Bun that context's globals come back broken (window.eval is an own property whose value is simply undefined -- 'TypeError: window.eval is not a function' -- and even built-ins like Map/Error resolve to undefined inside a script run there). Reproduced identically on every happy-dom major tested (16.0.0, 19.0.2, 20.12.0) under Bun; the exact same happy-dom 20.12.0 works correctly under real Node.js (window.eval is a real function, normal global semantics) with zero code change to check-render.mjs. A dead-end explored and reverted before finding this: happy-dom's newer enableJavaScriptEvaluation setting does make document.write()-inserted <script> tags auto-execute without window.eval, but even that runs each script in its own isolated scope (top-level function/var declarations do not attach to window) -- not usable for this harness's needs (window.switchModule must be reachable), so that direction was abandoned, not shipped. Fix: tests/test_html_render_harness.py's _js_runtime() (renamed from _bun()) now prefers a real `node` binary and falls back to `bun` only if no Node is on PATH; docs/AI_DEVELOPMENT_PROTOCOL.md's documented command switched from `bun ...` to `node ...`. check-render.mjs itself is unchanged. bun.lock/package.json unchanged (bun install/package resolution was never implicated, only Bun's vm module). items.title: CE.2 - Curated read-only command-primitive registry for checks
items.note: AUTOMATED_VALIDATED 2026-09-09 (docs/design/COMPLIANCE_CHECK_ENGINE.md section 5, decision D8; relay/NXS-LOCAL-0037). Shipped: configuration/command_primitives.py -- a static registry (CommandGateReview dataclass carrying all 10 network-device-command-gate points per entry: reason, action_class_id, vendor_platform_shell_context, timeout_seconds, retry_count, max_frequency_per_endpoint_minutes, session_reuse, unsupported_behavior, secret_output_risk, safe_telemetry) admitted only through register_primitive(), which fails closed if the declared action_class_id is not utils.action_taxonomy.CLASS_0_READ, if the literal command text matches a write-command-marker denylist, or if the numeric gate fields are out of a sane range -- a defense-in-depth check atop the human review, independent of it. Two concrete, gate-reviewed proof primitives, one per major vendor, each reusing an already-controlled transport/command rather than opening a new credential path (diagnostic-path law): cp_gaia_show_version_all (Check Point, reuses configuration.checkpoint_config_probe._connect/_run_exec and the exact 'clish -c show version all' the 0.6.1A probe already gate-reviewed) and pan_show_system_info (Palo Alto, reuses panorama.panorama_runtime_runner.get_api_key/op_cmd/fix_host and the exact op command configuration/panorama_config_collector.py already issues). PrimitiveExecutionTracker enforces the design's 'once per device per run' admission (in-memory, not a durable ledger -- explicitly deferred to a future promotion past opt-in probe mode, mirroring RECOVERY_OPERATIONAL_WRITE_LEDGER.md's precedent); run_check_point_primitives/run_palo_alto_primitives each open exactly one session/API key per probe batch and reuse it across every admitted primitive against that endpoint (session-reuse gate rule, test-proven via call-count assertions on a mocked transport). Redaction is uniform and raw-evidence-law compliant: every primitive's redact() returns only {bytes, lines, fingerprint_sha256} over the exact output text -- never raw content -- discarded by the caller in the same function that captured it. Admission wiring: new main.py --compliance-probe (application/workflows/compliance.py), modelled on --cp-config-probe -- reuses checkpoint_config_probe._pick_targets() for Check Point target selection (no second target-selection policy for the same evidence question) and the first already-discovered Panorama-managed serial for Palo Alto (best effort; AC-4 only requires 'CP and/or PAN'), both admitted through the existing utils.collection_executor admission coordinator (vendor='checkpoint'/'paloalto', so the existing 1-per-vendor budget applies unchanged), writes a new local-only redacted evidence artifact (output/compliance_probe_<timestamp>.json, sensitivity LOCAL_OPERATOR_SENSITIVE_NOT_SHAREABLE), and is mutually exclusive with every other collection/render/maintenance mode. Engine wiring (the 'exposed to the engine only as source namespace primitive.<primitive_id>' invariant, proven not just declared): 'primitive' added to utils.compliance_check_pack.SOURCE_NAMESPACES; utils.compliance_posture.build_compliance_posture/_subject_user_checks/_subject_evidence gained an additive primitive_facts_by_subject parameter (byte-identical when omitted, mirroring the existing crypto_facts_by_subject shape/precedent exactly) so a check pack can reference primitive.<id>.<field> today. Deliberately NOT wired into any normal-run caller (html_export.py unchanged) -- primitives execute only under the opt-in probe, never a normal collection run, per design section 5's 'Opt-in first' and this movement's explicit scope (promotion beyond opt-in probe mode is out of scope). diagnostic_runbooks_read_only's own runbook-catalog implementation was NOT built here (shares this registry per its own backlog note; clear extension points only -- PRIMITIVE_REGISTRY/primitives_for_vendor/run_*_primitives are vendor-generic and take an explicit primitives= list). Evidence: 33 new tests (tests/test_ce2_compliance_check_engine_primitives.py) covering registration rejection (write-marker commands, wrong action class, out-of-range gate values), tracker frequency/session-reuse limits (mocked transport call-count assertions), redaction (no raw text survives), and engine wiring (bare vs wired vs byte-identical-when-omitted); full suite 3126 passed / 27 skipped / 2 failed (the same pre-existing, unrelated DLP-token-collision pair in project/build_history.json + relay/NXS-LOCAL-0003, the accepted standing exception named in this movement's own merge_gate); repository privacy gate PASS/0 new findings vs origin/main; git diff --check clean. cp_device_interaction_safety (P0) closed 2026-08-25 (corrected 2026-08-30); the remaining prerequisite for promotion beyond opt-in probe mode is a real-environment validation gate against each primitive's real device output shape -- no live device reachable from this workspace, so REAL_ENV_VALIDATED/DONE stays owed and is added to CURRENT_STATE.md's real-environment-validation-owed list. items.title: CE.3 - Browser check editor + signed distributable org check packs
items.note: Design: docs/design/COMPLIANCE_CHECK_ENGINE.md section 6 (decision D9). A Compliance-module check editor: name a check, pick the evidence source from a browsable tree of WHAT WAS ACTUALLY COLLECTED (no blank text box), choose an operator, enter the expected value/pattern, test it LIVE against the last run (which subjects pass/fail), preview the coverage delta, save; every save audited (who/when/before/after). Signed org packs: detached signature + a publisher trust store so an org distributes vetted check packs without a product release (the dynamic/signed-pack direction of the 0.6.6B / 0.7.0 rule packs); invalid/untrusted -> rejected, fail-closed. CIS/PCI/BDDK starter packs shipped as signed builtin-adjacent packs the operator enables. Requires the app server + DEPLOY.1A OIDC/RBAC (only an authorised role creates/edits/loads checks) + a persistent store. items.title: CE.4 - Remediation checks (write-capable, HARD-GATED)
items.note: Design: docs/design/COMPLIANCE_CHECK_ENGINE.md sections 11-12. The product end-state is a write-capable device administration platform; the check model reserves an OPTIONAL remediation { primitive: <write_primitive_id>, parameters, verify_after: [steps] } block, unused and validator-rejected in CE.1-CE.3. CE.4 lets the engine, on an operator-authorised in-window run, execute the write primitive, re-run verify_after (reusing the CE.1 source/assert grammar verbatim), record an immutable audit entry, and auto-rollback on verify failure. A future REMEDIABLE sub-state on FINDING is additive. HARD-GATED on every prerequisite in docs/design/FAILOVER_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md section 10 - the same bar as failover_controlled_execution / OP.2: mature VERIFY/TRACE/RECOVER, the DEPLOY.1 server, DEPLOY.1A OIDC + an RBAC OPERATE role + full audit, the CP device-interaction-safety audit, the network-device command gate for every read AND write primitive, and a signed change-management / safety review with the network-security leads. items.title: CP preflight: add `cphaprob tablestat` (CCP unique-IP table) as an extra split-brain / control-link evidence source
items.priority: P1 -- valuable evidence, requires a new command-gate row + readiness-contract mapping before implementation
items.target: OP.0b follow-on (post S8 closure); implement only after PO approval of the gate row and the check mapping
items.note: PO request 2026-09-04 (real-environment ClusterXL S8-A, operator-supplied evidence). VENDOR SEMANTIC: `cphaprob tablestat` prints the CCP 'Unique IP's Table' -- for each cluster interface, which members are currently seen exchanging CCP on it (local member rows plus peer member rows, with per-interface IP and MAC). It answers a question the approved battery cannot: `cphaprob -a if` (CP-A4) proves the LOCAL link state of each cluster interface, not that CCP traffic is actually flowing to the peer on it. Operator scenario: one cluster interface physically disconnected while its link reports UP -- `cphaprob -a if` and `cphaprob stat` still look healthy, but the peer's row for that interface disappears from tablestat; that is the precursor to a split-brain election. So tablestat is positive, per-interface, cross-member CCP reachability evidence. WHY NOT ADDED NOW: it is a NEW device command, which is a hard-stop condition of the S8 campaign (new command authority = PO gate, `OP_0B_1_COMMAND_GATE_PACKAGE.md`), and its readiness mapping is a readiness-contract decision, not a parser fix. Nothing in the approved battery changed; `cphaprob -a if` (A4) and `cphaprob -ia list` (A5) are already approved reads and both now parse the real output shapes. WHAT IMPLEMENTATION NEEDS: (1) a gate row modelled on CP-A4 -- Vendor Check Point; Action class CLASS_0_READ; Execution plane device-direct SSH, existing per-member persistent Expert shell; Shell/context Expert direct, physical/VS0; Expected calls per member 1; Concurrency/timeout/retry as CP-A4 (NO_RETRY); Session reuse yes, same session and same INTER_COMMAND_DELAY_SECONDS pacing; Read-only evidence yes (`cphaprob tablestat` is a ClusterXL monitoring command); Evidence category F (link/control health) and/or the split-brain category. (2) SAFE RETAINED FIELDS ONLY -- the raw table carries per-interface IP addresses and MAC addresses: the parser must retain NO address, NO MAC, NO interface name; only bounded counts/booleans: number of cluster interfaces observed, number on which BOTH members are seen, number on which the peer member is absent, and whether the local member is seen on every required interface (cross-referenced only by count against CP-A4's `Required interfaces:`). Structural skeleton diagnostic applies if the shape is unrecognised. (3) READINESS MAPPING (PO decision, not to be invented): candidate checks are `no_split_brain` (peer absent on a required cluster interface = CCP not exchanged = election risk) and `control_sync_link_health` (per-interface CCP reachability, stronger than link state). The classification of 'peer row absent on a required interface' -- FAIL versus INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE -- must be decided against the frozen 'never KNOWN_BAD from absence' law: here the absence is inside the device's own positively-reported table, which is a different thing from a read that produced nothing, but the contract must say so explicitly before the code does. (4) VSX: physical/VS0 context only unless a per-VS semantic is separately established. (5) Tests: parser fail-closed on unknown shape; value-free retained fields (no IP/MAC survives); one call per member in the same shell; battery order and S4 command authority unchanged. Until this item is implemented, the readiness contract keeps its current (weaker) control-link evidence: link state, not CCP exchange. PO APPROVAL 2026-09-09: the Product Owner approved adding the `cphaprob tablestat` gate row (modelled on CP-A4, CLASS_0_READ, one call per member in the existing Expert session, NO_RETRY, value-free retained fields only) and asked for the readiness-contract mapping to be drafted in the same movement for review -- the mapping (FAIL vs INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE for peer-row-absent) is proposed with reasoning against the never-KNOWN_BAD-from-absence law, not silently decided. Dispatched as relay/NXS-LOCAL-0049. 2026-09-09 D-5: HELD until the PO runs cphaprob tablestat on hardware; engineer not resumed.

P0 before CLASS 2 (record now)'), which had no backlog item, no roadmap row and no design section anywhere in the repository. FAILOVER_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md section 10.1 item 4 requires a per-HA-entity lock held across preflight -> act -> verify. The lock that exists today is per PHYSICAL ENDPOINT -- utils.coordinator_backend.derive_lock_key(secret, 'endpoint', canonical_id), admitted by utils.collection_executor.CollectionCoordinator -- and two members of one cluster are two endpoints, so it is the wrong grain for an action whose subject is the cluster. MODEL (independent review 2026-09-04, docs/history/phase/OP_2_0_CONTROLLED_HA_OPERATION_ARCHITECTURE.md P8/P10): (1) the HA-entity lock IS the durable action record -- the store admits at most one record per operational_entity_id (CP ClusterXL group_id; CP VSX physical cluster parent; never a member, management address, SSH endpoint, API session or browser session) that is non-terminal or an unacknowledged OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, enforced by a create-race-safe uniqueness check; no new lock mechanism, key domain or table; (2) the existing per-endpoint coordinator admission (lease + vendor budget) is taken per device-contact stage -- the preflight, then precondition + submission + verification -- and NEVER across the human confirmation wait, because the lease is connection-lifetime (DEV.3.2) and the vendor budget (capacity 1) would otherwise block every collection of that vendor for an unbounded time; refused admission is ABORTED_PRE_MUTATION:member_busy, never a wait; (3) quarantine after OUTCOME_UNKNOWN is a derived predicate over the record store, lifted only by an authorized, audited acknowledgement -- a restart cannot lift it because reconciliation never rewrites a terminal state. Frozen by the product owner on 2026-09-04; implementation is OP.2.B's, a future movement behind OP.0b closure. items.title: Two PCP.1 registry tests fail deterministically on main: uuid4 call-count proof also counts the lock's owner token
items.target: PCP.1 (utils/device_registry.py + tests/test_pcp1_device_registry.py); no product behaviour change expected
items.note: Discovered 2026-09-05 while establishing a pre-change test baseline for NAV.1, in a sandbox that (unlike the PCP.1 session's) has pytest/lxml/paramiko installed. tests/test_pcp1_device_registry.py::test_duplicate_enroll_refused_before_device_id_generated and ::test_lock_contention_on_enroll_never_generates_a_device_id both monkeypatch dr.uuid.uuid4 and assert the call list is empty. utils/device_registry.py::_acquire_lock generates the lock's owner_token with uuid.uuid4() before the O_CREAT|O_EXCL attempt, so exactly one call is always recorded and both tests fail with [1] == []. Deterministic, reproducible on HEAD (310593e) with the navigation change stashed, and unrelated to NAV.1. Why it reached main: .github/workflows/validation.yml's fast PR `validate` job runs only a fixed smoke set (credential redaction, privacy gate, known safety gaps, frontend rendering boundary) and never ran this file; the `full-regression` job runs on push to main, i.e. after the merge. CURRENT_STATE.md's 'confirmed green by PR #83's fast PR CI' claim is therefore accurate about what that job ran and over-broad about what it proves for this file. The AC being proven ('no device_id is generated before the duplicate/lock refusal') is still correct and still holds -- the *proof technique* over-reaches by counting every uuid4 call in the process rather than the device_id one. Fix is a test-mechanism decision inside PCP.1's frozen section 21 contract (e.g. count only calls made after lock acquisition, or assert on the persisted record instead of the call count) and is deliberately NOT folded into the NAV.1 UI movement. RESOLVED 2026-09-06 (commit ebfe081, already on main before this movement dispatched): added a single narrow production seam, utils/device_registry.py::_generate_device_id(), used only for device_id generation and kept separate from _acquire_lock's own unrelated owner_token uuid4() call; both named tests repointed their monkeypatch at that seam instead of the module-wide dr.uuid.uuid4, so the call count no longer over-reaches. No frozen PCP.1 AC-1a..AC-15 behavior changed. This backlog entry's status field was left stale (still "planned") after that fix landed; NXS-LOCAL-0038 re-verified both tests pass deterministically (2 passed) and closes the status here. No further code change was needed or made on this branch.

items.title: M8.4 finding: CP config evidence snapshot metadata carries no host-key fingerprint, so the M8 trust-currency check can never affirmatively pass against real M8.3 evidence
items.target: configuration/checkpoint_config_collector.py::_collect_host (the shared, 'existing unmodified' physical-host collection primitive both the bulk collector and the M8.3 producer reuse)
items.note: Discovered while implementing M8.4 (console/registry_targets.py's identity-translation currency checks, frozen M8 contract section 7): one required condition is 'the current trusted-key fingerprint for the live registry endpoint agrees with producing_run_ref's captured fingerprint.' _collect_host does capture a live host-key fingerprint (host_row['host_key_fingerprint'] = key_fp) but never persists it into the CP config evidence snapshot's extra_metadata (configuration/checkpoint_config_collector.py, the store.write_text_snapshot(...) call inside _collect_host) -- so no resolvable producing_run_ref evidence written by any real M8.3 run today carries a host_key_fingerprint field. M8.4's own check therefore fails closed (never a vacuous pass) for every real relationship until this is fixed -- proven and pinned by tests/test_m8_4_m6_resolver_consumption.py::TestCurrencyFailuresFoldToIdentityTranslationRequired::test_todays_real_m8_3_evidence_shape_has_no_fingerprint_and_fails_closed. Not fixed in M8.4 itself per that movement's own scope boundary ('do not modify the M8.3 producer unless a material correctness defect makes M8.4 impossible' -- M8.4's own resolver logic is fully correct and testable via fixture evidence that does carry the field; the gap is in the shared collector's evidence-write path, not in M8.3's or M8.4's own code, and touching the shared, unmodified _collect_host primitive deserves its own explicit review rather than a scope-expanding side effect here). Proposed minimal fix: add "host_key_fingerprint": host_row.get("host_key_fingerprint") to the extra_metadata dict _collect_host already passes to store.write_text_snapshot for the physical-host artifact (PHYSICAL_ARTIFACT_TYPE only -- do not add it to the VSX context artifact, which has no independent host-key handshake of its own). This value is a SHA256: fingerprint, not raw key material or a credential -- consistent with this repository's existing host_key_fingerprint format and the M8 contract's own privacy law (fingerprints are the one piece of trust evidence M8.2/M8.3 already treat as safe to carry, e.g. utils/cp_ssh_trust.py::TrustedKeyLookupResult.fingerprints). UPDATE 2026-09-07: fixed on branch m8-evidence-host-key-fingerprint-not-persisted -- host_key_fingerprint now flows into the physical-host store.write_text_snapshot(...) extra_metadata exactly as proposed above; VSX context evidence intentionally unchanged. See project/build_history.json's m8_evidence_host_key_fingerprint_not_persisted record for full evidence. PR #103 MERGED to main 2026-09-07 (true merge commit 06e51d36a11ed2ecc8dfc4d7581656aa09c5c95d), Product Owner approved.

PRODUCT OWNER'S EXPLICIT REQUIREMENTS (verbatim intent preserved): (1) a real clickable app, not a terminal redraw loop; (2) it reads the orchestrator's own state, and the refresh interval must be changeable from inside the UI itself (persisted, not only a --interval CLI flag); (3) a list of all tasks/movements; (4) clicking one opens a full detail view; (5) at a glance: what is currently being developed, what has already been developed (done/merged), and what stage each active movement is at, grouped active-on-top / recently-done-in-the-middle / closed-at-the-bottom, not one flat list.

PRIOR ART SURVEYED (what comparable local dev-tool dashboards do, and what to borrow): CI/job dashboards (GitHub Actions run list, Airflow DAG-run UI, Prefect/Dagster run UI) all share the same shape -- a grouped/filterable run list with a colored status badge, a click-through detail view with a tabbed layout (overview / logs / timeline), and a live-tailing log pane. Process managers (pm2, Docker Desktop/Portainer, k9s) add the 'what's alive right now' angle: liveness derived from the actual OS-level process/container check, never from a timestamp alone -- confirms this movement's own finding that pid_alive, not heartbeat_at, is the only honest liveness signal today. The consistent architectural pattern across all of them for a single-user local tool: a thin local backend that already owns the ground truth (here: scripts/orchestrator.py's state dir + relay/*.json + each worktree's git status) exposes a small read JSON API; a static single-page frontend polls or subscribes to it; no user accounts, no multi-tenancy, bind to localhost only.

RECOMMENDED ARCHITECTURE (REQUIRED unless the engineer session finds a concrete blocker, reported via RELAY_QUESTION): (A) Backend -- a new `python3 scripts/orchestrator.py dashboard [--port N, default e.g. 8765] [--relay-dir] [--state-dir]` subcommand, stdlib-only (http.server/socketserver/wsgiref -- matches the existing 'no new third-party dependency' invariant already enforced for orchestrator.py and local_relay.py), bound to 127.0.0.1 only. It serves (a1) one static HTML/CSS/JS page (vanilla, no build step, single file or a small handful under a new scripts/dashboard_assets/ or similar -- no npm/webpack/node toolchain in this repo, do not introduce one), and (a2) a small JSON API reusing the existing status-computation functions (_status_row, _read_last_activity, _heartbeat_age_seconds etc.) rather than re-implementing them: GET /api/movements (grouped list), GET /api/movements/<id> (detail: full .nexus/approved_task.json acceptance criteria, complete relay entry history in order with actor+marker+timestamp+body, git worktree status --porcelain parsed into a human label, ahead/behind origin/main counts, open PR number+state+CI conclusion via `gh pr list --head <branch>` if `gh` is available -- degrade gracefully to 'n/a' if not, never crash), GET /api/movements/<id>/log (tail of engineer.summary.log, or engineer.log if the summary doesn't exist yet, capped at a reasonable byte count), GET/PUT /api/config (currently just {"poll_interval_seconds": N}, persisted to a small JSON file e.g. .nexus/dashboard_config.json at the repo root -- not per-worktree). (B) Frontend refresh: plain polling via fetch() at the UI-configurable interval is sufficient and simplest (avoid SSE/WebSocket complexity unless the engineer session judges it trivial with stdlib alone -- do not add a dependency for this). (C) Real per-movement 'stage' string (addresses a gap this Product Owner already found in the existing terminal watch): derive from git worktree status instead of trusting heartbeat_at alone -- e.g. 'not started yet' (only SESSION_START posted, no worktree changes), 'developing' (uncommitted changes present), 'resolving merge conflict' (UU/AA porcelain markers), 'ready to push' (committed, no PR yet), 'PR open, CI running/red/green' (via gh), 'merged' (relay CLOSED + PR merged). (D) heartbeat_at itself: either make it genuinely periodic (the spawned engineer process or a lightweight orchestrator-side poller updates it on a real signal) or rename/relabel it honestly in both the API and the UI so it is never presented as liveness -- pid_alive stays the authoritative liveness check either way. (E) Grouping in the UI: active (phase running, pid_alive true) on top; done-but-recent (phase done, e.g. within the last N hours or last N items) in the middle; closed/merged in a collapsed-by-default bottom section -- exactly the three-tier grouping the Product Owner asked for. (F) Detail view tabs/sections: Overview (objective, acceptance criteria, current stage, branch, worktree path, PR link), Relay history (the full ordered marker log -- this is the audit trail GOV.PO.3 already relies on, so surfacing it in the UI is pure value, no new data), Log (live-tailing engineer.summary.log with fallback to raw engineer.log). (G) Read-only by default, mirroring 'orchestrator watch' and 'local_relay.py watch' precedent -- no start/stop/resume/merge action buttons in this first version; that would be a new write surface crossing back into the two-touchpoint governance boundary (GOV.PO.3 section on human interaction points) and should be its own, separately-decided follow-up if ever wanted, not bundled in silently here.

OUT OF SCOPE for this movement (flag anything that looks like it needs these, do not build them here): authentication/multi-user support (single local user, no need); a build toolchain/npm dependency; write/action buttons (see (G)); mobile responsiveness beyond basic usability; historical analytics/charts beyond the three-tier list. ACCEPTANCE-SHAPE GUIDANCE for whoever turns this into a formal SESSION_START: reproduce the existing terminal watch's exact data shape as the JSON API's baseline (backward compatible, AC-5-style), add targeted tests for the new stage-derivation function and the config read/write endpoint in isolation (no need to test the frontend JS with a browser harness -- test the data/API layer, same testing philosophy relay/NXS-LOCAL-0013 used for its own watch loop).

=== AMENDMENT 2026-09-08 (supersedes item (G) 'read-only, no action buttons' above; the rest of the original architecture research still stands as background) ===
Product Owner-directed correction after external design review: a monitoring-only dashboard is not enough. What's actually needed is an interactive PO + Orchestrator workbench that surfaces what is expected of the Product Owner, routes the Product Owner's answer to the correct session, and lets the work continue from the same screen. Reading the 'two-touchpoint' principle (work selection, design decisions) as 'therefore read-only UI' was wrong -- work-selection and decision buttons ARE the interface for those exact two touchpoints, and a screen that lets the Product Owner change the poll interval persistently is already not purely read-only anyway. The scope correction below, written as the amendment to hand directly to the implementing engineer session (English, verbatim):

Amend orchestrator_interactive_dashboard_app from a monitoring-only dashboard to an interactive PO + Orchestrator workbench.

Preserve the existing local stdlib backend and vanilla JS frontend. Reuse the orchestrator and local relay as the execution and decision sources; do not introduce another scheduler or independent state model.

First delivery must include:
- A human-action inbox, ranked by blocked work and urgency.
- Concurrent movement cards with process status, explicit work stage, last observed activity, owner, and next action.
- Movement detail: acceptance criteria, conversation, events, diffs, tests, artifacts, worktree/session references, and preview links.
- Start/resume of authorized work, queued messages to the correct session, and observable message-delivery acknowledgments.
- Structured execution requests with action ID, exact operation, working directory, expected effects, and blocker source.
- Automatic routing of already-authorized engineering actions away from the PO role; ask the human only for an actual missing decision.
- Serialized integration visibility and existing authorized auto-merge.

Do not infer work stage from Git dirtiness or heartbeat. Do not claim access to unavailable agent transcripts or hidden reasoning. UI actions must use existing authorization rules, reject stale requests, and prevent duplicate execution. Platform denials remain explicit.

Acceptance demonstration: Track five concurrent movements; answer a pending design question; deliver a message to the correct worker; route an authorized command request; resume the affected work; open its produced UI/test artifact. Complete this flow without manual chat-to-chat copying or Git commands.

DETAILED LAYOUT (from the same design review, informative -- the implementing session may adapt presentation but should preserve the five sections and their stated actions):
Main screen, five sections top to bottom: (1) 'Awaiting you' -- decisions, permission blocks, design questions; which work each one is blocking; actions: answer, approve an option, defer, reject. (2) 'Running movements' -- the concurrent movements, owner, real stage, last progress, next step; actions: open detail, send a message, request pause, stop. (3) 'PO agenda' -- suggested NEXT, ready work, dependencies, why each is waiting; actions: start, prioritize, queue. (4) 'Integration queue' -- PRs awaiting review/test/merge and why each is waiting; actions: view findings, request a fix. (5) 'Recently completed / archive' -- what shipped, test result, PR, remaining debt if any; actions: open the result and the artifact/UI that was built. A small summary strip above all five: e.g. '5 running - 2 awaiting decision - 1 in integration.' Any movement that needs a decision must surface at the TOP of its group, not just get sorted into 'active' generically.

Detail panel (opens on click, right-hand pane), six tabs: Summary (what's being done, user-facing benefit, acceptance criteria, next step); Live activity (the agent's own posted progress notes, running command/test, latest result); Conversation (PO/engineer/reviewer messages, threaded, showing which message answered which); Changes (changed files, diff summary, branch/worktree, PR link); Evidence (test result, screenshot, render output, local UI preview); History (dispatch, correction, decision, retry, and integration events in order).

'Where is Claude actually running' must be answerable via the relation agent/session -> movement -> worktree -> current activity -- surfaced explicitly, not hidden. If the platform does not expose it, never fabricate a full terminal transcript or hidden reasoning trace to fill the gap -- posted messages and tool events are what's real and what should be shown.

The single most valuable feature: an executable-request card. Convert a 'I can't run this in a terminal, no permission' message into a card shaped like: 'Test run blocked / Movement: .../ Requested action: .../ Target environment/worktree: .../ Expected effect: .../ Blocker source: PO role restriction / missing dependency / platform policy' with buttons [Route to engineer] [Run the authorized action] [Reject]. Three distinct cases must be told apart: (1) the action is already authorized but reached the wrong role -- the orchestrator routes it to the engineer automatically, no question surfaces to the Product Owner at all; (2) a genuinely new human decision is needed -- show the action and its effect, record the choice to the relay, let the affected work continue; (3) a platform/organizational policy is the actual blocker -- show the real blocker; a UI button must never be presented as if it can override that policy. The button must send a registered action id, not free-form shell text typed in the browser -- the backend resolves the id to its already-recorded operation, argument set, and working directory, which is what prevents running in the wrong worktree and prevents a double-click from starting the same thing twice; if the underlying command has changed since the id was issued, the stale approval must not apply.

Live stage must never be inferred from git dirtiness alone: a dirty worktree does not mean 'writing code' and a clean one does not mean 'done'. Show three distinct fields -- Process status (running / exited / disconnected), Work stage (review / coding / testing / awaiting PO / integration), Last observed activity (e.g. 'test started 90s ago') -- with stage sourced from real orchestrator/engineer-posted events, heartbeat limited to meaning process reachability only, and 'last activity unknown' shown honestly when there is no evidence, never a fabricated progress percentage.

A message box is itself part of the work: every movement needs a 'send a note to this work' field, and the message's own delivery state must be visible: Saved -> delivered to session -> received by agent -> answered. If delivery to the currently-running session isn't supported, queue it for the next continuation/resume call and say so explicitly in the UI -- never show 'Sent' for a message the agent never actually read.

Security note carried over from the architecture review: once action buttons exist, localhost-only binding is not enough by itself -- add a session token plus Origin/CSRF checking, specifically so another web page open in the same browser cannot silently send commands to the local service without an extra confirmation screen.

Explicitly deferred past the first delivery: a fully embedded terminal, desktop packaging, a drag-and-drop workflow editor, and advanced charting -- none of those block the acceptance demonstration above.

Success criterion for this whole screen, stated by the Product Owner directly: 'I understood what work is waiting on me, I gave the answer it needed, and I saw the work continue on the same screen.'

=== PO SCOPE BOUNDARY 2026-09-08 (decided, not merely flagged -- Product Owner asked for a resolved, dispatch-ready item that will not need another design round; consulting the external reviewer ('Astra') again remains an option later, but is not required to proceed) ===
This backlog item's FIRST DISPATCH is bounded to the following. Anything not listed here is explicitly deferred (see 'DEFERRED' below), not silently included.

IN SCOPE, decided:
- Read+relay-write only. Every card/button in this first delivery (decision inbox, message box, structured executable-request card) ends by appending an entry to the movement's own relay file (a RELAY_DECISION, a queued note, or an equivalent structured instruction) -- none of them execute git/gh/shell directly from the dashboard backend. The existing, already-audited engineer dispatch path (orchestrator start / resume, gated by scripts/nexus_engineer_tool_gate.py) is what actually executes anything, exactly as it does today for a PO decision typed into a relay append. This closes the authorization-duplication risk: there is exactly one place permission logic lives.
- 'Automatic routing of an already-authorized action' and the 'Run the authorized action' button are ONE mechanism, not two: both resolve to 'append this instruction to the relay, so the next dispatch/resume picks it up.' Build it once.
- The five-section main screen, six-tab detail panel, decision inbox ranked by urgency, movement cards with process-status/work-stage/last-activity as three distinct fields (never inferred from git dirtiness alone, never a fabricated progress percentage), and the structured executable-request card shape -- all as specified in the AMENDMENT section above -- are IN SCOPE for this first dispatch.
- Message-delivery UI must default its copy to the state that is actually achievable today: 'Saved -> queued for next resume' as the normal, expected outcome -- not 'delivered to session' or 'received by agent', which require a live session-control channel this repository does not have (confirmed: orchestrator.py's --resume is a fresh respawn into the same worktree, not a reconnect to a running claude session -- relay/NXS-LOCAL-0015's own finding, 2026-09-08). Do not build or imply a live-delivery guarantee.
- Local stdlib backend + vanilla JS frontend, orchestrator/relay as the only state and decision sources, localhost-bound. Session token + Origin/CSRF checking is IN SCOPE for this first dispatch specifically because relay-write buttons already exist here (writing a RELAY_DECISION is a real action, not merely a read) -- do not defer this to a later 'once we add real action buttons' phase; that phase is now.

DEFERRED, explicitly out of scope for this dispatch (their own future backlog items if wanted, not part of this one):
- Any button that directly executes git/gh/shell from the dashboard backend itself (the earlier draft's 'Run the authorized action' as literal execution) -- stays relay-write-only per above until a specific, separately-authorized follow-up revisits it.
- The 'Evidence' tab's real content (screenshots, render output, local UI preview) -- ship the tab structurally (so the layout is future-proof) but it is allowed to show 'no artifact producer configured yet' rather than fabricated or empty-implying-broken content; wiring real screenshots/render output needs its own engineer-side output-contract addition (e.g. a documented .nexus/artifacts/ convention) first, not part of this dispatch.
- A fully embedded terminal, desktop packaging, drag-and-drop workflow editor, advanced charting (already deferred in the AMENDMENT above; restated here for a single source of truth).
- Any true live-session message channel (would require the orchestrator to persist and reconnect to a real claude session id -- a separate, larger movement if ever pursued; NOT bundled here).

This boundary is the final word for a first dispatch; the implementing engineer session should treat 'IN SCOPE' as build-it and 'DEFERRED' as report-if-tempted-to-build-it-anyway-via-RELAY_QUESTION, not as open questions requiring another Product Owner design round.

items.title: An engineer's own claude -p background task can outlive its process's turn, leaving staged-but-uncommitted work when the session exits without waiting
items.target: scripts/orchestrator.py::_spawn_engineer and/or the ENGINEER_PROMPT -- observed live during relay/NXS-LOCAL-0018 (PR #133 merge-conflict completion), 2026-09-08
items.note:
Real bug, observed live, not hypothetical. relay/NXS-LOCAL-0018's engineer session staged its merge-conflict-resolution changes (`git add`), then ran the full pytest regression via the claude CLI's own internal background-task mechanism (the run exceeded a 120s foreground timeout and was auto-moved to the background, e.g. `Command did not complete within its 120s timeout and was moved to the background (ID: bhpt1icqs)`). The session's own turn then ended (it printed a final assistant message and returned `result (success)`) WITHOUT waiting for that background task's completion notification -- the orchestrator's process record then showed `pid_alive: false` with the relay still at `SESSION_START` (no RELAY_ACK/NOTE/QUESTION/CLOSE ever posted) and the worktree left with everything staged but not committed (`git status --short` showed all changes in the index, nothing in `git log`). Recovered this time by a plain `orchestrator start` resume, which happened to pick the work back up cleanly (no data loss), but this is not guaranteed in general -- a background task producing a result the next resumed session never sees, or resuming mid-way through an unverified test run, is a real correctness gap for the standing 'green tests -> self-merge' authorization (relay#13): a session must not be able to reach a commit/push/merge step on the strength of a background test run it never actually waited to see the result of.

Fix direction (not yet designed in detail -- needs its own investigation before a SESSION_START is written): (a) the ENGINEER_PROMPT (scripts/orchestrator.py) could be strengthened to explicitly instruct every engineer session to never treat a long-running validation command as backgroundable -- always run the full regression suite as a foreground, awaited command, even past whatever timeout the CLI would otherwise auto-background it at (this may need a per-invocation flag/env var to raise or disable that auto-background threshold for engineer sessions specifically, if one exists -- verify before assuming); (b) alternatively/additionally, the orchestrator's own resume path (decide_start) could detect this specific pattern (index has staged-but-uncommitted changes, relay never advanced past SESSION_START, pid dead) and inject an explicit instruction into the resumed session's context to first check for and finish any prior staged-but-uncommitted work and any background task results before proceeding, rather than relying on the resumed session to figure this out unprompted (it did, this time, but that's not yet a guarantee). Report via RELAY_QUESTION if investigation finds the CLI gives no way to control or query this background-task behavior from outside the session.

Not urgent-blocking (recovery worked this time via a plain resume), but real and worth fixing before it causes an actual lost-work or premature-merge incident rather than just an extra resume cycle.

Priority raised P1 -> P0 on 2026-09-08 per explicit Product Owner direction: this is the one concrete engineering item among this session's PO-orchestration-efficiency findings (see PRODUCT_DIRECTION_RECORD.md section 14), and the standing relay#13 'green tests -> self-merge' authorization must not remain exposed to an unverified background test result. RESOLVED 2026-09-08 (relay/NXS-LOCAL-0019): confirmed pre-fix that ENGINEER_PROMPT did not instruct engineer sessions to run validation in the foreground regardless of the CLI's auto-background timeout, and that decide_start's resume path had no detection for the dead-pid-plus-staged-changes pattern. (a) ENGINEER_PROMPT strengthened: never treat a long-running validation command as backgroundable; run it foreground/awaited with an explicit long timeout; if the CLI backgrounds it anyway, wait for and read the real result before committing/pushing/merging. Investigated the installed claude CLI's own shipped behavior directly: it reads BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS (default 120000ms -- exactly the incident's '120s timeout') as the fallback timeout for a Bash-tool call without its own explicit timeout, and BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS, floored at that default, as the ceiling on an explicit one -- a real lever exists, so scripts/orchestrator.py::_spawn_engineer now sets BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS to 1_800_000 (30 min) in the engineer's own env (setdefault, never overriding an operator's own value), raising both; this does not disable auto-backgrounding outright (no such switch found) -- the prompt instruction is what the guarantee actually rests on. (b) decide_start's resume branch now calls new pure functions (relay_never_advanced_past_session_start / has_staged_uncommitted_changes / needs_resume_recovery_note; git status parsed, never spawned inside the pure functions) and, when the pattern matches, injects RESUME_RECOVERY_NOTE onto that one resume's prompt via _spawn_engineer's new extra_prompt_note parameter -- dispatch/refuse/ordinary-resume decisions are unchanged. Targeted tests added to tests/test_orchestrator.py; full one-shot regression green modulo two pre-existing, unrelated failures (see build_history.json).

items.title: .claude/nexus-engineer.settings.json never actually granted Edit/Write despite claiming default-allow -- every successful movement to date wrote files only via Bash
items.target: .claude/nexus-engineer.settings.json -- fixed live 2026-09-08, uncommitted pending a standalone PR
items.note: Found live 2026-09-08 while resuming NXS-LOCAL-0020 (gov_po_3_ci_privacy_gate_baseline_scoping): its Edit call on utils/repository_privacy.py was denied with 'this session has no approval surface to grant file-write permissions'. Root cause: scripts/orchestrator.py::_spawn_engineer passes `--permission-prompts none` (no human to answer a prompt, per relay/NXS-LOCAL-0015's own AC-1/AC-2/AC-3 comment), and .claude/nexus-engineer.settings.json's permissions block had only two `deny` entries (force-push) and no `allow` entries at all -- so every Edit/Write call, which requires approval by default, was silently auto-denied for the life of the process, contradicting the profile's own '_comment' claim of 'Default-allow (normal dev tools: Read/Edit/Write/Bash/Git)'. The same denial is visible in relay/NXS-LOCAL-0018's own engineer.log (Edit on project/build_history.json during merge-conflict resolution) -- that movement only succeeded because its engineer fell back to Bash-only file writes without flagging the denial as unusual. Fix: added `permissions.allow: ["Edit", "Write", "MultiEdit"]` to the profile (applied directly to the file on disk 2026-09-08 by explicit Product Owner action via chat '!' passthrough, since Claude Code's own auto-mode classifier refuses an AI-initiated Edit to a settings/tool-configuration file). Confirmed working: NXS-LOCAL-0020 resumed cleanly afterward. Still needs a standalone PR to persist the fix for future clones/CI -- the live fix is currently only an uncommitted change in the main checkout.

items.title: scripts/local_relay.py append accepts a relative --file path that silently shadows the correct canonical relay file with a new local copy inside the engineer's own worktree
items.target: scripts/local_relay.py::_resolve_relay_file / append CLI -- observed live on NXS-LOCAL-0021 (orchestrator_interactive_dashboard_app), 2026-09-08
items.note:
NXS-LOCAL-0021's engineer posted its AC-2 design-note RELAY_NOTE to a NEW file at <worktree>/relay/NXS-LOCAL-0021-orchestrator-interactive-dashboard-app.json instead of the canonical relay/ file the orchestrator spawned it against (env NEXUS_RELAY_FILE/NEXUS_CANONICAL_RELAY_DIR were set correctly at spawn time, per relay/NXS-LOCAL-0015's own --add-dir fix). Likely cause: `scripts/local_relay.py append`'s `--file` argument, when given a relative path, silently overrides the correct absolute env-var default and resolves relative to the engineer's cwd (the worktree root) per `_resolve_relay_file(explicit) -> explicit or env`, landing in a brand-new worktree-local relay/ file rather than erroring. The canonical relay file was left un-advanced (stuck at seq 1 SESSION_START, next_actor engineer) while the worktree's shadow copy silently accumulated the real conversation (seq 2 RELAY_NOTE, status AWAITING_PO) -- invisible to the PO/orchestrator until manually discovered and copied over by hand. Recovered manually this time (no lost content), but this is a real footgun: nothing currently stops a relative --file from creating a divergent shadow relay file, and the ENGINEER_PROMPT does not explicitly warn against passing --file at all when the environment default is already correct. Fix direction (not yet designed): reject or warn on a --file value that does not resolve to the same absolute path as NEXUS_RELAY_FILE when both are present, or resolve --file relative to NEXUS_CANONICAL_RELAY_DIR rather than cwd, or simply strengthen the ENGINEER_PROMPT to never pass --file explicitly when the env default is already set.

RESOLVED 2026-09-08 (NXS-LOCAL-0026): implemented reject-on-mismatch in `_cmd_append` -- when `NEXUS_RELAY_FILE` is set and an explicit `--file` is also given, append now refuses (EXIT_USAGE) unless `os.path.abspath(--file) == os.path.abspath(NEXUS_RELAY_FILE)`, instead of silently operating on the mismatched path. No `--file` (env default) and an absolute `--file` matching the env var are unchanged. Regression coverage added to tests/test_local_relay_protocol.py (the module's actual test file; the movement's own AC-3 named a not-yet-existing tests/test_local_relay.py) reproducing the exact NXS-LOCAL-0021 shape (NEXUS_RELAY_FILE/NEXUS_CANONICAL_RELAY_DIR set, relative --file that would previously resolve against cwd) plus a mismatch case and an env-unset passthrough case; also added an autouse env-clearing fixture to that test file since the ambient NEXUS_RELAY_FILE a real orchestrated engineer session exports was leaking into and breaking pre-existing tests once the mismatch check existed.

items.title: Private Replay -- agent-operated privacy-filtered test environment derived from real collection, for the coding agent to exercise the product UI/workflows without seeing real device data
items.target: docs/design/PRIVATE_REPLAY_ARCHITECTURE.md -- FROZEN -- PRODUCT OWNER APPROVED, 2026-09-08, Phase A only (offline exporter + PRIVATE_REPLAY + SYNTHETIC_SCENARIO). Phase B (LIVE_PRIVATE, agent-mediated real collection) stays explicitly deferred/unauthorized within that same document. Delivery slice 1 (dependency inventory + typed privacy/fidelity policy + isolated replay provider design) DELIVERED 2026-09-09 (relay/NXS-LOCAL-0027) -- see updated note. Next dispatchable unit: delivery slice 2 (Phase A exporter -- the offline typed exporter, package validator and relationship checks, extending utils/support_bundle.py's primitives, using synthetic inputs first).
items.note:
Objective: let a coding agent (Claude) drive real UI/menu/workflow testing against neXus to reproduce real customer-topology bugs, without the agent ever seeing real device identities, credentials or raw evidence content. FROZEN as of 2026-09-08 for Phase A only: PRIVATE_REPLAY (agent uses an immutable HMAC-pseudonymized dataset derived from a real collection, extending utils/support_bundle.py's existing Tokenizer) and SYNTHETIC_SCENARIO (agent uses fabricated edge cases -- stale peer, timeout, trust mismatch -- absent from the real environment). LIVE_PRIVATE (agent-triggered real collection via a trusted local execution service) is Phase B, deferred design only, not authorized by the freeze -- requires its own separate Product Owner authorization and explicit reconciliation with docs/AI_DEVELOPMENT_PROTOCOL.md's network-device command gate + utils/action_taxonomy.py before any dispatch.

This session's (2026-09-08) counter-review was accepted in full and folded into the frozen document: (1) offline-first sequencing (Phase A ships before any live-collection design is even authorized, not bundled with the exporter as originally proposed); (2) reuse of the existing AI-initiated-device-command gate rather than a parallel authorization mechanism; (3) isolation testing required from the agent's own actual tool perspective (Read/Bash/env-inspection/process-inspection against a dummy service with synthetic canaries), not just API-malformed-request testing. See the frozen document's own 'Counter-review disposition' section.

Priority raised P0 2026-09-08 per explicit Product Owner direction, scoped to Phase A delivery slices 1-3 only. Phase B stays a separate, later, separately-prioritized item -- this P0 does not cover it.
